residencyRequirements.description: Either party must be domiciled in Nigeria at the time of filing (MCA s.2). A wife who has been ordinarily resident in Nigeria for at least 3 years immediately preceding the petition is deemed domiciled in Nigeria (MCA s.7(b)). Any person domiciled in Nigeria may file in the High Court of any state or of the FCT (MCA s.2(3), s.114); the FCT High Court is the usual venue when either party resides within the Federal Capital Territory.

waitingPeriod.description: No mandatory waiting period after filing. The court grants a Decree Nisi, which becomes a Decree Absolute after 3 months (MCA s.58); where there are children under 16, subject to the court's s.57 declaration on arrangements for them. Cannot petition within 2 years of marriage unless leave is granted for exceptional hardship (MCA s.30); the bar does not apply to petitions based on wilful refusal to consummate, adultery, or s.16(1)(a) (s.30(2)).

twoYearBar.description: A petition for dissolution shall not be filed within two years of the date of marriage unless the court grants leave on grounds of exceptional hardship to the petitioner or exceptional depravity on the part of the respondent (MCA s.30). The bar does not apply to petitions based on wilful refusal to consummate (s.15(2)(a)), adultery (s.15(2)(b)) or s.16(1)(a), or to cross-proceedings (MCA s.30(2)).

noFault.name: 2-Year Separation with Consent
noFault.description: The parties have lived apart for a continuous period of at least two years immediately preceding the presentation of the petition and the respondent does not object to the grant of a decree.

noFault.name: 3-Year Separation without Consent
noFault.description: The parties have lived apart for a continuous period of at least three years immediately preceding the presentation of the petition.

fault.name: Wilful Refusal to Consummate
fault.description: Since the celebration of the marriage the respondent has wilfully and persistently refused to consummate the marriage.

fault.name: Adultery
fault.description: Since the celebration of the marriage the respondent has committed adultery and the petitioner finds it intolerable to live with the respondent.

fault.name: Intolerable Behaviour
fault.description: Since the celebration of the marriage the respondent has behaved in such a way that the petitioner cannot reasonably be expected to live with the respondent.

fault.name: Desertion for One Year
fault.description: The respondent has deserted the petitioner for a continuous period of at least one year immediately preceding the presentation of the petition.

fault.name: Failure to Comply with Restitution Order
fault.description: The respondent has, for a period of not less than one year, failed to comply with a decree of restitution of conjugal rights made under the Act.

fault.name: Presumption of Death (Absent 7 Years)
fault.description: The other party to the marriage has been absent for such time and in such circumstances as to provide reasonable grounds for presuming death; absence for at least seven years with no reason to believe the other party alive within that period is sufficient proof (MCA s.16(2)(a)).

basic.name: Petition for Dissolution of Marriage
basic.description: Initiates the divorce proceeding in the High Court under the Matrimonial Causes Act

basic.name: Affidavit in Support of Petition
basic.description: Sworn affidavit verifying the facts stated in the petition

basic.name: Marriage Certificate
basic.description: Original or certified true copy of the marriage certificate under the Marriage Act

legalCitations.code: Matrimonial Causes Act 1970, Cap M7 LFN 2004
legalCitations.description: Federal statute — governs dissolution of marriages contracted under the Marriage Act
Welfare of the child — adopted by the FCT

filingFees.notes: Filing fees vary by court registry. Additional fees for service of process and motion filing.

childSupportGuidelines.guidelines: Matrimonial Causes Act s.71; Child Rights Act 2003
childSupportGuidelines.notes: No statutory formula — the court considers the means and needs of the parties and the welfare of the child.

spousalSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may order maintenance for either spouse, having regard to means, earning capacity, and conduct of the parties.

decreeProcess.decreeNisi: Court grants Decree Nisi after hearing the petition on its merits.
decreeProcess.decreeAbsolute: Decree Nisi becomes Decree Absolute automatically by force of law 3 months after it is made (MCA s.58); no application is needed. Where there are children under 16, the decree does not become absolute until the court has declared it is satisfied with the arrangements for their welfare (MCA s.57).
